findings.issue: The position prompt relies on a “shaded return line” that is not a rink marking or separately rendered object.
findings.evidence: exp26-u11-004-q9 asks to move above “the shaded return line”; its setup only supplies YOU (10,4), F2 (14,-3), and D1 (12,0.5), with no rendered line.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact question patch: replace prompt with "Move YOU to a support point above the direct return lane between your old position and F2." Replace explanation with "This point gives F2 a new support relationship while keeping D1 visible; the lane is inferred from the named players, not an unrendered shade."

findings.issue: Both the communication key and position target send the gold defender toward the wrong net.
findings.evidence: The briefing says Navy attacks +x/right and YOU is gold returning toward the right net; q7 keys “tracking F2 toward the left net” and q9 asks “between F2 and the left net” (F2 is navy at x17, YOU x12).
findings.recommendedChange: Exact patches: q7 option a text -> "D1 has F1; I am tracking F2 toward the right net". q9 prompt -> "Move YOU between F2 and the right net." q9 explanation -> "This point improves the defended net-side relationship to F2 and keeps F1 visible; the recovery route remains conditional on F2’s movement."

findings.issue: The reset destination moves YOU farther toward +x even though the briefing requires returning to the neutral-zone side of the right blue line.
findings.evidence: The setup has YOU at (10,-3) and says YOU is beyond the right blue line; q9 reference is (12.4,-3.4), which moves farther right. The supplied catalog version uses an illustrative neutral-side point at (6,-3).
findings.recommendedChange: Exact patch: keep the prompt, replace reference with {"x":6,"y":-3}, and replace explanation with "This point places YOU on the neutral-zone side of the right blue line for this practice reset while keeping F1 visible; it is illustrative, not a formal offside verdict."

findings.issue: The multi-select key excludes a third live check that the prompt reasonably allows.
findings.evidence: q2 asks which two checks make a re-offer useful, but option c, “Whether the same route is still blocked after you move,” is also a valid check; the explanation itself says matching the old route can keep the line blocked.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact question patch: change prompt to "Which two positive signs make a re-offer useful?" and replace option c with {"id":"c","text":"Whether D1 has become a teammate"}; retain answer ["a","b"].

findings.issue: The position key describes the destination as below the rebound, but the reference is above the puck on the y axis.
findings.evidence: The puck is at (23,-5), while q4 reference is (22.1,-4.1); with the source coordinate convention, -4.1 is above -5. The prompt says “below the rebound.”
findings.recommendedChange: Exact patch: replace prompt with "Move YOU to an approach point just above the rebound that keeps the net and D1 visible." Replace explanation with "This point approaches the loose puck from above while keeping the net-side defender in view."

findings.issue: The scene key calls D1 behind YOU, but D1 is farther up ice on the +x attack.
findings.evidence: Navy attacks +x; YOU is at (-8,-4) and D1 is at (-2,2). q1 keys “D1” for “Which player is behind YOU,” although x=-2 is ahead of x=-8.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact question patch: replace prompt with "Which player is ahead of YOU in this neutral-zone picture?"; retain answer ["b"] and replace explanation with "D1 is ahead of YOU on the +x direction and sits inside the route."

findings.issue: The multi-select key marks an incorrect defensive aim as correct.
findings.evidence: q2 asks what an inside approach tries to preserve. Option b says “A chance to chase F2 wide immediately,” but the explanation says F2 still needs a scan; the correct preservation is the middle/net route in option a.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact patch: change answer from ["a","b"] to ["a"]. Replace explanation with "Inside positioning protects the middle and route to the net while showing the carrier a wall-side route; F2 remains a separate scan, not an immediate chase."

findings.issue: The key contradicts the attack direction and coordinates.
findings.evidence: Gold attacks -x; YOU is at (13,2) and F1 at (15,4). F1 is to the +x side of YOU, so it has not moved beyond YOU toward the left net as the prompt states.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact question patch: replace prompt with "Which attacker is closer to YOU after the missed reach?"; retain answer ["a"] and replace explanation with "F1 is the nearer attacker to YOU in this freeze; the picture does not by itself establish a movement path toward the left net."

findings.issue: The coaching key sends the gold attack toward the wrong net.
findings.evidence: The briefing says Gold attacks -x/left. q2 option a says “F2’s route toward the right net,” while q4 and the rest of the scene defend the left-net route.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact patch: replace option a text with "F2’s route toward the left net"; retain answer ["a","b"] and replace explanation with "The uncovered runner toward the left net and D1’s pressure on F1 define the backcheck job."

findings.issue: The nearest-player key contradicts the supplied coordinates, even though the coach separately assigns F2 as retriever.
findings.evidence: Puck is at (23,-9); YOU at (21,-5) is about 4.5 m away, while F2 at (19,-9) is 4 m away. q1 says F2 is closer without reconciling the explicit retriever assignment.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact question patch: replace option a text with "The coach assigned F2 as the retriever" and replace explanation with "F2 has a different first job because the coach assigned that retrieval; YOU supports from above even though the frozen distances are close." Retain answer ["a"].

findings.issue: One distractor in each affected question is cartoonishly impossible or unsafe instead of a credible U11 misconception, reducing the quality of the decision contrast.
findings.evidence: The affected distractors are: exp26-u11-003-q8 “Pass to yourself through D1”; exp26b-u11-001-q5 “Stop reading and skate into D1”; exp26b-u11-004-q5 “Skate directly into F2’s path”; exp26b-u11-006-q5 “Skate through D1 to the net”; exp26b-u11-007-q5 “Whether D1 has become a teammate”; exp26b-u11-021-q5 “A pass behind the net to no one.”
findings.recommendedChange: Exact option patches: exp26-u11-003-q8 option c -> "Keep offering the same lane without changing your angle"; exp26b-u11-001-q5 option c -> "Carry into the middle without checking whether D1 has closed it"; exp26b-u11-004-q5 option c -> "Stay on the old return line without checking F2’s route"; exp26b-u11-006-q5 option c -> "Keep chasing the rebound as if D1 had not reached it"; exp26b-u11-007-q5 option c -> "Keep the same carry without rechecking F2"; exp26b-u11-021-q5 option c -> "Hold the puck without checking whether F2 becomes reachable".

limits: AI coaching review, not human approval; no rendered-image certification.
All 250 assigned questions were inspected in their complete supplied scenarios; static frames cannot certify movement, timing, possession outcomes, formal offside calls or legal contact.
